metadata.title: How to invest in transformational innovation

content.text:
Investing.com -- Investors seeking long-term growth should focus on artificial intelligence, power infrastructure, and healthcare innovation, according to UBS, which recommends diversified exposure to these sectors amid rising valuations and market volatility.
The November 16 research report identified three major investment themes expected to influence equity market performance over the coming years: AI, power and resources, and longevity.
AI-related capital expenditure is projected to reach $1 trillion in 2026 and $1.4 trillion in 2027, supported by increased spending from major technology companies and growing adoption of autonomous AI agents.
Yet elevated valuations, uncertainty surrounding U.S. policy, and diverging corporate performance have increased the risks associated with concentrated investments.
A balanced approach across the AI supply chain is favored, including selected semiconductor manufacturers, hardware providers, major technology companies, and more defensive industry segments.
Power infrastructure represents another long-term opportunity as data center expansion accelerates electricity demand.
Annual investment in power and grid infrastructure is expected to reach $3 trillion by 2030, creating opportunities in renewable energy, nuclear power, grid resilience, industrial automation, and critical minerals.
Data centers could account for 9% of U.S. electricity consumption by 2035, compared with approximately 4% currently, according to BloombergNEF estimates cited in the report.
Policy changes, project delays and execution risks could create volatility, although strong order backlogs and investment pipelines support the sector's longer-term outlook.
Healthcare innovation forms the third investment theme, particularly treatments designed to extend healthy lifespans.
The global longevity market is forecast to generate $8 trillion in annual revenue by 2030, up from $5.3 trillion in 2023.
Obesity-drug revenues are also expected to grow approximately 12% annually through 2030, supported by broader patient access, expanding insurance coverage, and new oral treatments.
